I will keep to the cropping pattern I know best: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. In Quzhou County, that is the safest way for me to use the whole year, protect my grain income, and avoid taking on crops that need more labor, more market timing, or more technical skill. I do not have formal schooling, so I will not gamble on unfamiliar varieties or complicated field management. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because they are common, dependable, and give me better yield stability. For wheat, I will focus on base fertilizer, a spring topdressing of nitrogen, 2 irrigations if water is available, and a few pesticide sprays only when pressure is visible. For maize, I will plant right after wheat harvest, keep fertilizer balanced but nitrogen a bit higher, irrigate mainly at key growth stages, and control weeds and insects with a limited number of sprays. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical, fast, and fits how I would manage the field at my age with a straightforward routine.
